name: Sonar Sweep
summary: A deep-sea 404 page: a glowing sonar scope sweeps the seabed for pages that still answer
about: A full not-found page set 404 metres down, with light rays, drifting sea snow, swaying kelp and a whale gliding past. At its heart is a phosphor sonar scope: the sweep lights up echoes, pings ripple out, and each contact you chart becomes a link back to the surface. One red signal never answers, because that is the page that sank.
how: The scope boots up while the depth gauge dives to 404 m, then a demo pings and charts contacts by itself
Type a page name in Search the deep and press Ping; the ring spreads out and locks on the matching echo
Click any blip on the scope, or an echo in the Contacts list, to chart it and read its bearing and range
Each charted contact shows its address and a Surface here link in the readout under the scope
Chart all six to complete the survey: bubbles burst and light floods down from the surface
The red No signal mark is the missing page; lock on it for a quick way home, or use Go back
